Round-trip was never asserted, so both were invisible: the output looks correct and cannot be run | `mdl/executor/cmd_settings.go` (`describeSettings`, `writeSettingsConfiguration`), `mdl/executor/cmd_settings_languages.go`, plus the upserts that make replay possible: `alterSettingsLanguageUpsert` and `CreateConfigurationStmt.CreateOrModify` (`mdl/ast/ast_settings.go`, `mdl/visitor/visitor_settings.go`, `createConfiguration`) | Emit **upsert** verbs — `create or modify configuration`, `alter settings LANGUAGE add or modify` — because the plain CREATE/ADD forms refuse what is already there, which is right for a hand-written script and wrong for a described project replayed onto itself. Note `CREATE (OR (MODIFY\|REPLACE))?` was **already** in the grammar generically, so `create or modify configuration` parsed and silently behaved as a plain CREATE: a documented upsert that answered "already exists". Order matters — `DefaultLanguageCode` is validated against the enabled list, so it must come AFTER the languages — and every option must be named, because MODIFY touches only what it names. **Test both directions**: replay onto the SAME project (unit byte-identical, and the run reports `Unchanged`, not `Updated`) and onto a BLANK one (settings document identical field for field). The same-project replay is what exposes verb dishonesty; the blank-project replay is what exposes a missing upsert. Known boundary: settings that REFERENCE module documents (`AfterStartupMicroflow`, a constant override) legitimately dangle on a project without them — mxbuild says CE1613 — and mxcli neither warns nor validates those references, which is tracked separately. Example `mdl-examples/doctype-tests/languages.mdl` |
